seoTitle: TradingView Horizontal Line Shortcut for Faster Charting
metaDescription: Learn the fastest keyboard shortcut to draw a horizontal line in TradingView, customize it, and lock support and resistance levels for quicker analysis.
intro: Manually clicking through menus to mark support and resistance can slow down your chart work, especially when you're tracking multiple setups. This guide shows the quickest way to activate the horizontal line tool using a keyboard shortcut, then customize and lock your levels efficiently. It's aimed at intraday and swing traders who want faster charting workflows.

steps.heading: Use the horizontal line shortcut
steps.body: Trigger the keyboard shortcut for the horizontal line tool to instantly activate it without navigating through the drawing tools menu.

steps.heading: Draw the level quickly
steps.body: Click on the chart at the price level you want to mark, and the horizontal line will be placed instantly.

steps.heading: Customize line settings
steps.body: Adjust the color and thickness of the line to make important levels stand out clearly on your chart.

steps.heading: Lock and manage lines
steps.body: Lock the line in place once it's positioned correctly so it doesn't get accidentally moved while you continue analyzing the chart.

steps.heading: Apply tips to speed up your drawing workflow
steps.body: Combine the shortcut with saved templates or default settings to mark multiple levels quickly across different charts.

faq.question: Do keyboard shortcuts work the same across all TradingView plans?
faq.answer: Keyboard shortcuts are generally available across the platform, though it's worth confirming any plan-specific differences in your account.

faq.question: Can I change the default color of horizontal lines drawn with the shortcut?
faq.answer: Yes, you can adjust the default style settings so new horizontal lines use your preferred color and thickness automatically.

faq.question: Why should I lock a horizontal line after drawing it?
faq.answer: Locking prevents the line from being accidentally dragged or moved while you're working elsewhere on the chart.

faq.question: Is using shortcuts faster than the drawing tools menu?
faq.answer: Yes, shortcuts let you skip the menu entirely, which speeds up marking multiple levels compared to manually clicking through tool options each time.
